# Codex Adversarial Review — Career #102 + #104 POST-FIX Diff (2026-06-02)

## Context

This is the **second** Codex pass on the Career System refactor + repurpose work for issues #102 and #104. The first Codex pass (`codex-adversarial-career-102-refactor-2026-06-02.output.md`) ran against the pre-fix diff and surfaced 1 MED + 1 LOW. A parallel 5-dimension Claude deep-review workflow surfaced 15 confirmed findings (2 HIGH, 4 MED, 9 LOW), of which 7 were actioned and the rest refuted with rationale.

**This review targets the FIXES themselves** — the changes we made in response to Codex pass 1 + the deep-review, plus the #104 implementation. None of the post-fix code has been independently reviewed.

## Diff under review (all relative to working dir `c:/Users/mikew/source/repos/TAOM`)

### Issue #102 fixes layered on top of the original refactor

- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/UI/AbilityHudController.cs` — Codex MED: added `private ScreenBase _attachedScreen;` captured at `TryInitialize()` after `AddLayer`, consumed in `Cleanup()` instead of re-reading `ScreenManager.TopScreen`. Deep-review HIGH: wrapped the engine-touching teardown (RemoveLayer / ReleaseMovie / VM.OnFinalize) in `try { ... } catch (Exception ex) { _logger?.LogWarning(...) } finally { /* field-reset block */ }` so a throw cannot leave `_hudInitialized=true` on the Singleton.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/IAbilityActivationController.cs` — Deep-review MED: replaced the single-outcome `AbilityActivationOutcome` enum with a flags-style `AbilityActivationResult { bool JustBecameReady; bool Activated; bool Charging; }` struct so the legacy dual-toast UX is preserved when the ability becomes ready AND V is pressed on the same frame.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/AbilityActivationController.cs` — Tick rewritten to return the struct; sets `JustBecameReady=true` BEFORE returning even when `Activated` also fires on the same frame; deduped `IsAbilityReady` lookups (one local); tightened `dt` semantics comment (Codex LOW: mission-simulation delta, not wall-clock).
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/CareerPerkMissionBehavior.cs` — Switch over `AbilityActivationOutcome` replaced with three independent `if (result.X)` branches; hoisted `hasCareer` to one call at top of `OnMissionTick`; `OnEndMission` rewritten with **per-step** `try/catch` around each of `_hudController.Cleanup()`, `_activationController.Reset()`, `_abilityService.ClearAll()`, `CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAll()` so a throw in one does not abort the others. Net file is now 139 lines.
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/CareerSystem/AbilityActivationControllerTests.cs` — 13 tests rewritten for the flags struct API; new regression test `Tick_ReadyAndVPressedSameFrame_FlagsBothJustBecameReadyAndActivated` proves the deep-review MED fix.

### Issue #104 Option B implementation (new on this diff)

- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Domain/AbilityTemplateData.cs` — new `public float CooldownReduction { get; set; }` property (default 0), copied in copy ctor.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Domain/AbilityTuningConfig.cs` — `GlobalTuning` gained `public float MinCooldownSeconds { get; }` (default 5f) and an optional ctor param.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/CareerConfigProvider.cs` — `ParseGlobalTuning` now parses an optional `min_cooldown_seconds` XML attribute. Validations: rejects non-finite (`NaN`/`±Infinity`), negative, and values > the cooldown itself. Falls back to default with warning. Pattern mirrors the existing `cooldown_seconds` parser (see `feedback_clamp_nan_infinity_propagates.md` — bug has shipped three times).
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/CareerAbility.cs` — new `public void AdjustCooldown(float reductionSeconds, float minCooldownSeconds)`. No-op for charge-based abilities, NaN/Infinity-safe, negative-reduction-rejected (treat as zero), negative-min-clamped to 0. Sets `CooldownRemaining = Math.Max(min, CooldownRemaining - reduction)`.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/ICareerAbilityService.cs` + `CareerAbilityService.cs` — new `ApplyCooldownAdjustment(string heroStringId, float reductionSeconds, float minCooldownSeconds)` method that delegates to the ability's `AdjustCooldown`. Logs warning for unknown hero.
- `Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/AbilityEffectExecutor.cs` — `Execute` reads `template.CooldownReduction` from the post-mutation template; if `> 0f`, calls `_abilityService.ApplyCooldownAdjustment(heroId, reduction, MinCooldownSeconds)` BEFORE running the per-archetype effect executor + the registerContext callback. Added `ICareerAbilityService _abilityService` to ctor.
- `Main/_Module/ModuleData/career_system/taom_career_choices.xml` — 98 `<Mutation property="MaxCharge" ... value="-20"/-30"/>` entries rewritten to `<Mutation property="CooldownReduction" ... value="-6"/-9"/>` via `tools/rename_maxcharge_to_cooldownreduction.py` (50× -20→-6 + 48× -9). Preserves the 1.5× tier ratio.
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/CareerSystem/CooldownReductionTests.cs` — 15 new tests covering: AbilityTemplateData default + copy-ctor, GlobalTuning default + ctor overload, CareerAbility.AdjustCooldown happy + floor + zero + negative + NaN + Infinity + NaN min + charge-based no-op, CareerAbilityService.ApplyCooldownAdjustment unknown-hero + happy + floor.

## Adversarial review surface — attack these specifically

1. **Flags-struct caller audit.** The replacement of `AbilityActivationOutcome` enum with `AbilityActivationResult` flags struct is a public API change. Confirm:
   - There are NO other callers of `IAbilityActivationController.Tick` besides `CareerPerkMissionBehavior.OnMissionTick` (grep the repo).
   - There are NO other references to the now-deleted `AbilityActivationOutcome` enum.
   - `CareerPerkMissionBehavior.OnMissionTick` correctly handles the new mutually-non-exclusive semantics. Specifically: the legacy switch-case ensured `Activated` and `Charging` were mutually exclusive (one switch case fires); the new code uses `if (result.Activated) {...} else if (result.Charging) {...}`. Confirm `Activated` and `Charging` are still mutually exclusive *by construction in the controller* — i.e., the controller cannot set both true on the same tick. Read `AbilityActivationController.cs:48-72` carefully.
   - The new test `Tick_ReadyAndVPressedSameFrame_FlagsBothJustBecameReadyAndActivated` is the only flag-coincidence test. Are there other simultaneous-flag scenarios I should test? (`JustBecameReady + Charging`? — is that physically possible if the ability is ready but V is pressed while charging? Should be impossible because "ready" and "on cooldown" are mutually exclusive.)

2. **OnEndMission per-step try/catch ordering.** Read `CareerPerkMissionBehavior.cs:113-130`. The order is `_hudController.Cleanup()` → `_activationController.Reset()` → `_abilityService.ClearAll()` → `CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAll()`. Is there any ordering dependency where a failure in step N would CORRUPT step N+1 if N+1 still runs? (Example: if HUD cleanup throws partway through, does subsequent ClearAll see a corrupted dict?) The previous straight-line order had implicit "fail-fast"; per-step try/catch makes the cleanup more resilient but exposes ordering assumptions that may not hold.

3. **AbilityEffectExecutor cooldown adjustment ordering.** Read `AbilityEffectExecutor.cs:47-95`. The flow is:
   ```
   1. Lookup careerId, career, raw template, mutated template.
   2. Compute duration + radius.
   3. If template.CooldownReduction > 0: _abilityService.ApplyCooldownAdjustment(heroId, reduction, min)
   4. Construct MissionAbilityExecutionContext.
   5. registerContext.Invoke(context)  -- adds to host's _activeContexts
   6. executor.Execute(context)  -- runs the per-archetype effect (may throw)
   7. InformationManager.DisplayMessage(...)  -- yellow toast
   8. PlaySound / PlayParticle if non-empty
   ```
   
   Question: the `ApplyCooldownAdjustment` runs in step 3 — BEFORE the `executor.Execute(context)` at step 6 that may throw. If `executor.Execute` throws, the cooldown has already been shortened but the buffs/particles never applied. Is this a real regression vs the legacy (where cooldown was set to full `CooldownDuration` and never adjusted)? Walk the failure timeline.

4. **`CareerAbility.AdjustCooldown` semantic ambiguity.** Read `CareerAbility.cs:62-77`. Current implementation: `if (reductionSeconds <= 0f) return;`. This rejects negative AND zero. But also: `if (float.IsNaN(reductionSeconds) || float.IsNaN(minCooldownSeconds)) return;` — and `if (float.IsInfinity(reductionSeconds) || float.IsInfinity(minCooldownSeconds)) return;`. Order matters: the NaN check must precede the `<=` check because NaN comparisons always return false (NaN <= 0f is false, so a NaN would slip past the early return WITHOUT the explicit NaN guard above). Confirm the guard ordering is correct.

5. **MinCooldownSeconds parsing — sign-flipped designer typo.** `CareerConfigProvider.ParseGlobalTuning:444-456` rejects `< 0f`. Confirm a designer who typos `min_cooldown_seconds="-5"` (intending to "allow no minimum") gets the rejection-with-warning, not silently mis-applied. Also confirm `min_cooldown_seconds > cooldown_seconds` (e.g., min=60s but cooldown=30s) is rejected — current code has `else if (parsedMin > seconds)`.

6. **XML rewrite script audit.** Read `tools/rename_maxcharge_to_cooldownreduction.py`. The regex is `r'property="MaxCharge" calculator="flat" value="(-20|-30)"'`. Is there any sibling attribute in the XML that could have matched? Run `git diff Main/_Module/ModuleData/career_system/taom_career_choices.xml` and visually confirm the only diff lines are the 98 mutations — no neighbor lines were accidentally re-flowed. Also confirm the regex is anchored tightly enough that a future `value="-20.5"` (parsed by a sibling Mutation type) wouldn't be touched.

7. **CHANGELOG of the surviving legacy `MaxCharge` property.** `AbilityTemplateData.MaxCharge` was NOT removed (the property is still on the model). The mutation pipeline (`MutationService.ApplyMutation` via reflection) would still write to it if any future XML mutation targets it. Is this an acceptable "dead but harmless" state, or should we remove the property entirely to forbid future regressions? Consider the rule `feedback_no_aspirational_enum_values.md` ("don't keep reserved fields without a producer + consumer").

## Cross-feature regression risks

8. **HUD Cleanup try/finally and the `_hudInitialized` reset.** Read `AbilityHudController.cs:95-126` carefully. In the `finally` block, every field is nulled INCLUDING `_hudInitialized = false`. The `try` block runs three engine calls in sequence. If `RemoveLayer` throws, do we ever WANT `_hudInitialized` to remain true? Argue both sides — there's an outside chance that leaving `_hudInitialized=true` post-throw would let the next mission's `TryInitialize` short-circuit and at least keep the player from seeing a worse error. (Current design is defensively "reset everything and try fresh next mission" — confirm this is correct.)

9. **First Codex review's `_attachedScreen` ownership.** When `TryInitialize` runs the second time (idempotent guard via `_hudInitialized`), the early-return is at line 54. But on the NEW path (post-Cleanup), `_attachedScreen` is now null (cleared in finally). If somehow `_hudInitialized` is true but `_attachedScreen` is null (no path makes this true under normal flow, but defensive review): does Cleanup crash on the null deref? Current code is `if (_attachedScreen != null && _hudLayer != null) _attachedScreen.RemoveLayer(_hudLayer);` — short-circuit handles it. Confirm.

10. **MinCooldownSeconds = 0 edge case.** If a designer sets `min_cooldown_seconds="0"`, can a stack of CooldownReductions cause `CooldownRemaining = 0`, causing `IsReady` to immediately return true on the same frame, causing the player to fire the ability instantly with no cooldown ever displayed? Walk: `AdjustCooldown` clamps to `max(0, CooldownRemaining - reduction)`. The HUD updates next tick. Activation-controller's `JustBecameReady` would fire on the next tick. The player CAN spam-activate, but the cooldown does run between activations. Is this acceptable behavior? (Probably yes — if a designer chooses 0 floor, they get a 0 floor.)

+    // Issue #104 Option B — per-activation cooldown reduction in seconds. The 98 dead MaxCharge
+    // mutations in taom_career_choices.xml were repurposed to target this property after the
+    // cooldown rework (#103) made MaxCharge unread for CooldownOnly abilities. Calculator
+    // convention: <Mutation property="CooldownReduction" calculator="flat" value="-6"/> for
+    // a 6-second reduction (note the negative sign — the FlatCalculator subtracts |value| from
+    // the running sum; designers reading the XML should think of the negative value as
+    // "shortens cooldown by 6s"). Effective cooldown is floored at GlobalTuning.MinCooldownSeconds.
+    public float CooldownReduction { get; set; }
+
     public AbilityTemplateData() { }

 }

     public float CooldownSeconds { get; }
 
-    public GlobalTuning(float cooldownSeconds)
+    // Issue #104 Option B — minimum effective cooldown after CooldownReduction mutations.
+    // Floor prevents designer-stack-up cheese (50 careers × multiple keystones could in theory
+    // sum to a 30s+ reduction; clamp ensures the global cooldown is still observed at minimum 5s).
+    public float MinCooldownSeconds { get; }
+
+    public GlobalTuning(float cooldownSeconds, float minCooldownSeconds = 5f)
     {
         CooldownSeconds = cooldownSeconds;
+        MinCooldownSeconds = minCooldownSeconds;
     }
 
-    public static GlobalTuning Default => new GlobalTuning(30f);
+    public static GlobalTuning Default => new GlobalTuning(30f, 5f);
 }

   1: namespace TAOM.Features.CareerSystem.Abilities;
   2: 
   3: // Per-frame V-key + cooldown state machine extracted from CareerPerkMissionBehavior.OnMissionTick
   4: // (Issue #102). Pure logic + injected adapters -- no TaleWorlds statics, fully unit-testable.
   5: //
   6: // Result fields per tick (flags-style — multiple can be true simultaneously):
   7: //   no career               -> all false
   8: //   cooldown finished       -> JustBecameReady = true (one-shot until next Activated)
   9: //   V pressed, ready        -> Activated = true (re-arms the JustBecameReady flag); JustBecameReady
  10: //                              is also true on the same frame if the cooldown completed THIS frame
  11: //   V pressed, on cooldown  -> Charging = true (throttled to once per 2s)
  12: public class AbilityActivationController : IAbilityActivationController
  13: {
  14:     private const float ChargingMessageThrottleSeconds = 2f;
  15: 
  16:     private readonly ICareerAbilityService _abilityService;
  17:     private readonly IAbilityInputAdapter _input;
  18:     private readonly IMissionTimeProvider _time;
  19: 
  20:     private bool _abilityReadyNotified;
  21:     private float _lastChargingMessageTime = -ChargingMessageThrottleSeconds;
  22: 
  23:     public AbilityActivationController(
  24:         ICareerAbilityService abilityService,
  25:         IAbilityInputAdapter input,
  26:         IMissionTimeProvider time)
  27:     {
  28:         _abilityService = abilityService;
  29:         _input = input;
  30:         _time = time;
  31:     }
  32: 
  33:     public AbilityActivationResult Tick(float dt, string heroStringId, bool hasCareer)
  34:     {
  35:         var result = default(AbilityActivationResult);
  36:         if (!hasCareer) return result;
  37: 
  38:         // dt is the mission-simulation delta from MissionBehavior.OnMissionTick -- NOT wall-clock.
  39:         // v1.4.5 Mission.OnTick (verified via Codex #102) scales dt by Scene.TimeSpeed and
  40:         // splits fast-forward into multiple 0.1s sub-ticks before the final tick. The cooldown
  41:         // domain wants mission-time (30s of fighting, not 30s of real-world wall-clock), so this
  42:         // is the correct semantic. Tick(dt) is invoked per-frame and not batched (Codex Review
  43:         // #31 caught a single-bucket accumulator dropping elapsed time on long frames).
  44:         _abilityService.Tick(heroStringId, dt);
  45: 
  46:         // Deep-review #102 LOW — hoist a single isReady local. Two IsAbilityReady calls per
  47:         // activation frame is sub-microsecond waste but trivially deduplicated.
  48:         var isReady = _abilityService.IsAbilityReady(heroStringId);
  49: 
  50:         if (isReady && !_abilityReadyNotified)
  51:         {
  52:             _abilityReadyNotified = true;
  53:             result.JustBecameReady = true;
  54:         }
  55: 
  56:         if (_input.IsActivationKeyPressed())
  57:         {
  58:             if (isReady)
  59:             {
  60:                 _abilityService.ActivateAbility(heroStringId);
  61:                 _abilityReadyNotified = false; // re-arm for the NEXT cooldown completion
  62:                 result.Activated = true;
  63:                 return result;
  64:             }
  65: 
  66:             var now = _time.CurrentTime;
  67:             if (now - _lastChargingMessageTime >= ChargingMessageThrottleSeconds)
  68:             {
  69:                 _lastChargingMessageTime = now;
  70:                 result.Charging = true;
  71:             }
  72:         }
  73: 
  74:         return result;
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     public void Reset()
  78:     {
  79:         _abilityReadyNotified = false;
  80:         _lastChargingMessageTime = -ChargingMessageThrottleSeconds;
  81:     }
  82: }

  23:     private readonly IAbilityHudController _hudController;
  24:     private readonly IAbilityEffectExecutor _effectExecutor;
  25:     private readonly IModLogger _logger;
  26: 
  27:     private bool _loggedMissionStart;
  28:     private readonly List<MissionAbilityExecutionContext> _activeContexts = new List<MissionAbilityExecutionContext>();
  29: 
  30:     public override MissionBehaviorType BehaviorType => MissionBehaviorType.Other;
  31: 
  32:     public CareerPerkMissionBehavior(
  33:         ICareerDataService dataService,
  34:         ICareerAbilityService abilityService,
  35:         IAbilityActivationController activationController,
  36:         IAbilityHudController hudController,
  37:         IAbilityEffectExecutor effectExecutor,
  38:         IModLogger logger)
  39:     {
  40:         _dataService = dataService;
  41:         _abilityService = abilityService;
  42:         _activationController = activationController;
  43:         _hudController = hudController;
  44:         _effectExecutor = effectExecutor;
  45:         _logger = logger;
  46:     }
  47: 
  48:     public override void OnMissionTick(float dt)
  49:     {
  50:         if (Campaign.Current == null) return;
  51:         var hero = CharacterObject.PlayerCharacter?.HeroObject;
  52:         if (hero == null) return;
  53: 
  54:         var heroId = hero.StringId;
  55:         var hasCareer = _dataService.HasCareer(heroId);
  56: 
  57:         if (!_loggedMissionStart)
  58:         {
  59:             _loggedMissionStart = true;
  60:             var careerId = _dataService.GetCareerStringId(heroId);
  61:             _logger?.LogInfo($"CareerSystem: Mission started — hero='{heroId}' hasCareer={hasCareer} career='{careerId ?? "none"}'");
  62:         }
  63: 
  64:         _hudController.TryInitialize();
  65:         _hudController.Refresh(heroId);
  66: 
  67:         var result = _activationController.Tick(dt, heroId, hasCareer);
  68:         if (result.JustBecameReady)
  69:         {
  70:             InformationManager.DisplayMessage(new InformationMessage(
  71:                 "Career ability is ready! Press V to activate.", Colors.Green));
  72:         }
  73:         if (result.Activated)
  74:         {
  75:             _logger?.LogInfo($"CareerSystem: Ability activated for hero '{heroId}' via V key");
  76:             _effectExecutor.Execute(heroId, _activeContexts.Add);
  77:         }
  78:         else if (result.Charging)
  79:         {
  80:             var remaining = (int)Math.Ceiling(_abilityService.GetCooldownRemaining(heroId));
  81:             if (remaining < 1) remaining = 1;
  82:             InformationManager.DisplayMessage(new InformationMessage(
  83:                 $"Career ability still charging — {remaining}s remaining.", Colors.Gray));
  84:         }
  85: 
  86:         var currentTime = Mission.Current?.CurrentTime ?? 0f;
  87:         for (var i = _activeContexts.Count - 1; i >= 0; i--)
  88:         {
  89:             _activeContexts[i].Tick(currentTime);
  90:             if (_activeContexts[i].IsExpired)
  91:                 _activeContexts.RemoveAt(i);
  92:         }
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     public override void OnAgentRemoved(Agent affectedAgent, Agent affectorAgent, AgentState agentState, KillingBlow blow)
  96:     {
  97:         if (agentState != AgentState.Killed && agentState != AgentState.Unconscious) return;
  98:         if (Campaign.Current == null) return;
  99: 
 100:         var hero = CharacterObject.PlayerCharacter?.HeroObject;
 101:         if (hero == null) return;
 102: 
 103:         var mainAgent = Mission.Current?.MainAgent;
 104:         if (affectedAgent == mainAgent)
 105:         {
 106:             CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearBuff(hero.StringId);
 107:             CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAllAllyBuffs();
 108:             _activeContexts.Clear();
 109:         }
 110:     }
 111: 
 112:     protected override void OnEndMission()
 113:     {
 114:         // Deep-review #102 MED — singleton-controller-per-mission-behavior lifetime asymmetry.
 115:         // Each cleanup op runs in its own try/catch so a throw from one (the HUD layer's
 116:         // RemoveLayer is the most plausible per the screen-mismatch RCA) does not abort the
 117:         // others, which would leave singleton state stuck across mission boundaries.
 118:         try { _hudController.Cleanup(); }
 119:         catch (Exception ex) { _logger?.LogWarning($"CareerSystem: OnEndMission _hudController.Cleanup() threw — {ex.Message}"); }
 120: 
 121:         try { _activationController.Reset(); }
 122:         catch (Exception ex) { _logger?.LogWarning($"CareerSystem: OnEndMission _activationController.Reset() threw — {ex.Message}"); }
 123: 
 124:         try { _abilityService.ClearAll(); }
 125:         catch (Exception ex) { _logger?.LogWarning($"CareerSystem: OnEndMission _abilityService.ClearAll() threw — {ex.Message}"); }
 126: 
 127:         try { CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAll(); }
 128:         catch (Exception ex) { _logger?.LogWarning($"CareerSystem: OnEndMission CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAll() threw — {ex.Message}"); }
 129: 
 130:         _logger?.LogInfo("CareerSystem: Mission ended — clearing abilities");
 131:         _loggedMissionStart = false;
 132:         _activeContexts.Clear();
 133:     }
 134: 
 135:     public override void OnAgentDeleted(Agent affectedAgent)
 136:     {
 137:         CareerAbilityBuffTracker.ClearAllyBuff(affectedAgent.Index);
 138:     }
 139: }

  12: namespace TAOM.Features.CareerSystem.Abilities;
  13: 
  14: // Per-activation effect pipeline extracted from CareerPerkMissionBehavior.ExecuteAbilityEffect
  15: // (Issue #102). Boundary class -- allocates MissionAbilityExecutionContext (touches
  16: // Mission.Current.MainAgent) and emits the InformationManager "activated" toast. The host
  17: // MissionBehavior owns the _activeContexts expiration list and passes registerContext so the
  18: // allocated context joins it.
  19: public class AbilityEffectExecutor : IAbilityEffectExecutor
  20: {
  21:     private readonly ICareerDataService _dataService;
  22:     private readonly ICareerRegistry _registry;
  23:     private readonly ICareerConfigProvider _configProvider;
  24:     private readonly CareerAbilityEffectRegistry _effectRegistry;
  25:     private readonly IMutationService _mutationService;
  26:     private readonly ICareerHeroAdapterFactory _adapterFactory;
  27:     private readonly Abilities.ICareerAbilityService _abilityService;
  28:     private readonly IModLogger _logger;
  29: 
  30:     public AbilityEffectExecutor(
  31:         ICareerDataService dataService,
  32:         ICareerRegistry registry,
  33:         ICareerConfigProvider configProvider,
  34:         CareerAbilityEffectRegistry effectRegistry,
  35:         IMutationService mutationService,
  36:         ICareerHeroAdapterFactory adapterFactory,
  37:         Abilities.ICareerAbilityService abilityService,
  38:         IModLogger logger)
  39:     {
  40:         _dataService = dataService;
  41:         _registry = registry;
  42:         _configProvider = configProvider;
  43:         _effectRegistry = effectRegistry;
  44:         _mutationService = mutationService;
  45:         _adapterFactory = adapterFactory;
  46:         _abilityService = abilityService;
  47:         _logger = logger;
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     public void Execute(string heroStringId, Action<MissionAbilityExecutionContext> registerContext)
  51:     {
  52:         var careerId = _dataService.GetCareerStringId(heroStringId);
  53:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(careerId)) return;
  54: 
  55:         var career = _registry.GetCareer(careerId);
  56:         if (career == null) return;
  57: 
  58:         var rawTemplate = _configProvider.GetAbilityTemplate(career.AbilityTemplateId);
  59:         var template = MutateTemplate(rawTemplate, heroStringId);
  60: 
  61:         var duration = template?.Duration ?? 8f;
  62:         var radius = template?.Radius ?? 10f;
  63: 
  64:         // Issue #104 Option B — apply per-activation CooldownReduction (from designer choice
  65:         // mutations). Floored at GlobalTuning.MinCooldownSeconds. Called BEFORE Execute so the
  66:         // HUD pip on the very next tick reflects the adjusted cooldown.
  67:         if (template != null && template.CooldownReduction > 0f)
  68:         {
  69:             var min = _configProvider.GetAbilityTuning().Global.MinCooldownSeconds;
  70:             _abilityService.ApplyCooldownAdjustment(heroStringId, template.CooldownReduction, min);
  71:         }
  72: 
  73:         var mainAgent = Mission.Current?.MainAgent;
  74:         var context = new MissionAbilityExecutionContext(
  75:             heroStringId, duration, radius, mainAgent, Mission.Current, _logger);
  76: 
  77:         // Register the context BEFORE executor.Execute so any partial restores scheduled inside
  78:         // ApplyAoeBuff iterations are still tickable by the host even if a later iteration throws.
  79:         // Deep-review #102 considered swapping this; verdict was REFUTED — the swap leaks queued
  80:         // restores from completed iterations.
  81:         registerContext?.Invoke(context);
  82: 
  83:         var executor = _effectRegistry.GetExecutor(careerId);
  84:         executor.Execute(context);
  85: 
  86:         var abilityName = new TextObject(career.DisplayName).ToString();
  87:         InformationManager.DisplayMessage(new InformationMessage(
  88:             $"{abilityName} activated!", Colors.Yellow));
  89: 
  90:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(template?.SoundEffect))
  91:             context.PlaySound(template.SoundEffect);
  92:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(template?.ParticleEffect))
  93:             context.PlayParticle(template.ParticleEffect);
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     private AbilityTemplateData MutateTemplate(AbilityTemplateData rawTemplate, string heroId)
  97:     {
  98:         if (rawTemplate == null) return null;
  99:         if (Campaign.Current == null) return rawTemplate;
 100: 
 101:         var hero = CharacterObject.PlayerCharacter?.HeroObject;
 102:         if (hero == null || hero.StringId != heroId) return rawTemplate;
 103: 
 104:         var heroAdapter = _adapterFactory.Create(hero);
 105:         return _mutationService.MutateAbility(rawTemplate, heroAdapter, _dataService, _registry);
 106:     }
 107: }

  57:         if (CurrentCharge > MaxCharge)
  58:             CurrentCharge = MaxCharge;
  59:     }
  60: 
  61:     // Issue #104 Option B — shorten the active CooldownRemaining by reductionSeconds (clamped
  62:     // to floor minCooldownSeconds). No-op for charge-based abilities (the cooldown machinery
  63:     // doesn't run). NaN/Infinity/negative inputs are rejected so a bad XML mutation cannot
  64:     // produce a frozen state machine or a 0s cooldown bypass (see feedback_clamp_nan_infinity_propagates.md).
  65:     public void AdjustCooldown(float reductionSeconds, float minCooldownSeconds)
  66:     {
  67:         if (ChargeType != ChargeType.CooldownOnly) return;
  68:         if (float.IsNaN(reductionSeconds) || float.IsNaN(minCooldownSeconds)) return;
  69:         if (float.IsInfinity(reductionSeconds) || float.IsInfinity(minCooldownSeconds)) return;
  70:         if (reductionSeconds <= 0f) return;
  71:         if (minCooldownSeconds < 0f) minCooldownSeconds = 0f;
  72: 
  73:         var effective = Math.Max(minCooldownSeconds, CooldownRemaining - reductionSeconds);
  74:         CooldownRemaining = effective;
  75:     }
  76: }

   1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
   2: """Issue #104 Option B — repurpose 98 dead MaxCharge mutations in taom_career_choices.xml as
   3: CooldownReduction. After the cooldown rework (#103), template.MaxCharge is unread for
   4: CooldownOnly abilities (all 50 careers use cooldown-based gating). Designers editing -20/-30
   5: entries were silently misled. This script:
   6: 
   7:   - Renames property="MaxCharge" → property="CooldownReduction"
   8:   - Rescales value="-20" → value="-6"  (20% × 30s base = 6s reduction per tier-1 keystone)
   9:   - Rescales value="-30" → value="-9"  (30% × 30s base = 9s reduction per tier-2/3 keystone)
  10:   - Preserves the 1.5× ratio between the two tiers (was -30/-20 = 1.5, now -9/-6 = 1.5)
  11: 
  12: Run with --dry-run first to see the diff; --apply mutates the file in place.
  13: """
  14: 
  15: import argparse
  16: import re
  17: import sys
  18: from pathlib import Path
  19: 
  20: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
  21: XML_PATH = ROOT / "Main" / "_Module" / "ModuleData" / "career_system" / "taom_career_choices.xml"
  22: 
  23: # Match  property="MaxCharge" calculator="flat" value="-20"   (or -30)
  24: # Whitespace and attribute order are pinned to the actual file layout.
  25: PATTERN = re.compile(r'property="MaxCharge" calculator="flat" value="(-20|-30)"')
  26: 
  27: 
  28: def replace(match):
  29:     raw = match.group(1)
  30:     new_value = "-6" if raw == "-20" else "-9"
  31:     return f'property="CooldownReduction" calculator="flat" value="{new_value}"'
  32: 
  33: 
  34: def main():
  35:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
  36:     parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="Write changes to disk")
  37:     parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Show what would change (default)")
  38:     args = parser.parse_args()
  39: 
  40:     if not args.apply and not args.dry_run:
  41:         args.dry_run = True
  42: 
  43:     if not XML_PATH.exists():
  44:         print(f"ERROR: {XML_PATH} not found", file=sys.stderr)
  45:         sys.exit(1)
  46: 
  47:     original = XML_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  48:     matches = PATTERN.findall(original)
  49:     minus_20 = sum(1 for m in matches if m == "-20")
  50:     minus_30 = sum(1 for m in matches if m == "-30")
  51:     total = minus_20 + minus_30
  52: 
  53:     print(f"Found {total} MaxCharge mutations: {minus_20} × -20, {minus_30} × -30")
  54:     if total != 98:
  55:         print(f"WARNING: expected 98 mutations, found {total}", file=sys.stderr)
  56: 
  57:     mutated = PATTERN.sub(replace, original)
  58:     new_count_minus_6 = mutated.count('property="CooldownReduction" calculator="flat" value="-6"')
  59:     new_count_minus_9 = mutated.count('property="CooldownReduction" calculator="flat" value="-9"')
  60: 
  61:     print(f"After rewrite: {new_count_minus_6} × -6, {new_count_minus_9} × -9")
  62:     if new_count_minus_6 != minus_20:
  63:         print(f"FAIL: -20 → -6 count mismatch ({new_count_minus_6} vs {minus_20})", file=sys.stderr)
  64:         sys.exit(2)
  65:     if new_count_minus_9 != minus_30:
  66:         print(f"FAIL: -30 → -9 count mismatch ({new_count_minus_9} vs {minus_30})", file=sys.stderr)
  67:         sys.exit(2)
  68: 
  69:     if args.apply:
  70:         XML_PATH.write_text(mutated, encoding="utf-8")
  71:         print(f"OK: wrote {XML_PATH}")
  72:     else:
  73:         print("DRY RUN — pass --apply to commit")
  74:

 332: 
 333:     private void LoadAbilityTuningXml()
 334:     {
 335:         var path = Path.Combine(_pathService.ModuleDataPath, "career_system", "taom_ability_tuning.xml");
 336:         if (!File.Exists(path))
 337:         {
 338:             _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: ability tuning file not found at {path} — using defaults");
 339:             _abilityTuning = AbilityTuningConfig.Default;
 340:             return;
 341:         }
 342: 
 343:         try
 344:         {
 345:             var doc = XDocument.Load(path);
 346:             var root = doc.Root;
 347:             if (root == null)
 348:             {
 349:                 _abilityTuning = AbilityTuningConfig.Default;
 350:                 return;
 351:             }
 352: 
 353:             var globalEl = root.Element("Global");
 354:             var global = ParseGlobalTuning(globalEl);
 355: 
 356:             var infEl = root.Element("Infantry");
 357:             var infantry = infEl != null
 358:                 ? new InfantryTuning(
 359:                     ParseFloat(infEl, "damage_bonus", 15f),
 360:                     ParseFloat(infEl, "damage_reduction", 10f),
 361:                     ParseFloat(infEl, "radius", 50f))
 362:                 : InfantryTuning.Default;
 363: 
 364:             var rngEl = root.Element("Ranged");
 365:             var ranged = rngEl != null
 366:                 ? new RangedTuning(
 367:                     ParseFloat(rngEl, "speed_bonus", 15f),
 368:                     ParseFloat(rngEl, "ranged_damage_bonus", 20f),
 369:                     ParseFloat(rngEl, "draw_speed_bonus", 20f))
 370:                 : RangedTuning.Default;
 371: 
 372:             var cavEl = root.Element("Cavalry");
 373:             var cavalry = cavEl != null
 374:                 ? new CavalryTuning(
 375:                     ParseFloat(cavEl, "mount_speed_bonus", 20f),
 376:                     ParseFloat(cavEl, "charge_damage_bonus", 25f),
 377:                     ParseFloat(cavEl, "damage_bonus", 10f))
 378:                 : CavalryTuning.Default;
 379: 
 380:             _abilityTuning = new AbilityTuningConfig(global, infantry, ranged, cavalry);
 381:             _logger.LogInfo($"CareerSystem: Loaded ability tuning — Global(cooldown={global.CooldownSeconds}s) Infantry(dmg={infantry.DamageBonus},red={infantry.DamageReduction},r={infantry.Radius}) Ranged(spd={ranged.SpeedBonus},dmg={ranged.RangedDamageBonus},draw={ranged.DrawSpeedBonus}) Cavalry(mspd={cavalry.MountSpeedBonus},chrg={cavalry.ChargeDamageBonus},dmg={cavalry.DamageBonus})");
 382:         }
 383:         catch (Exception ex)
 384:         {
 385:             _logger.LogError($"CareerConfig: failed to load ability tuning XML: {ex.Message}");
 386:             _abilityTuning = AbilityTuningConfig.Default;
 387:         }
 388:     }
 389: 
 390:     private const float MaxCooldownSeconds = 3600f;
 391: 
 392:     private GlobalTuning ParseGlobalTuning(XElement globalEl)
 393:     {
 394:         if (globalEl == null) return GlobalTuning.Default;
 395: 
 396:         var raw = globalEl.Attribute("cooldown_seconds")?.Value;
 397:         if (raw == null) return GlobalTuning.Default;
 398: 
 399:         if (!float.TryParse(raw, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var seconds))
 400:         {
 401:             _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global cooldown_seconds=\"{raw}\"> is not a number — falling back to {GlobalTuning.Default.CooldownSeconds}s");
 402:             return GlobalTuning.Default;
 403:         }
 404: 
 405:         // float.TryParse admits NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity. The range checks below evaluate false for NaN
 406:         // (NaN comparisons always yield false), which would let a NaN cooldown reach CareerAbility and
 407:         // permanently break the activation gate. Reject non-finite values explicitly.
 408:         if (float.IsNaN(seconds) || float.IsInfinity(seconds))
 409:         {
 410:             _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global cooldown_seconds=\"{raw}\"> is not a finite number — falling back to {GlobalTuning.Default.CooldownSeconds}s");
 411:             return GlobalTuning.Default;
 412:         }
 413: 
 414:         if (seconds <= 0f)
 415:         {
 416:             _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global cooldown_seconds=\"{seconds}\"> must be > 0 — falling back to {GlobalTuning.Default.CooldownSeconds}s");
 417:             return GlobalTuning.Default;
 418:         }
 419: 
 420:         if (seconds > MaxCooldownSeconds)
 421:         {
 422:             _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global cooldown_seconds=\"{seconds}\"> exceeds maximum of {MaxCooldownSeconds}s — falling back to {GlobalTuning.Default.CooldownSeconds}s");
 423:             return GlobalTuning.Default;
 424:         }
 425: 
 426:         // Issue #104 Option B — min_cooldown_seconds is optional; floor for designer CooldownReduction
 427:         // mutations. Default 5s. Same NaN/Infinity/range guards as cooldown_seconds (see
 428:         // .claude/rules/csharp-architecture.md "Config Providers MUST Validate" + memory
 429:         // feedback_clamp_nan_infinity_propagates.md — the rule has shipped three times now).
 430:         var minRaw = globalEl.Attribute("min_cooldown_seconds")?.Value;
 431:         var minSeconds = GlobalTuning.Default.MinCooldownSeconds;
 432:         if (minRaw != null)
 433:         {
 434:             if (!float.TryParse(minRaw, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var parsedMin))
 435:                 _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global min_cooldown_seconds=\"{minRaw}\"> is not a number — falling back to {minSeconds}s");
 436:             else if (float.IsNaN(parsedMin) || float.IsInfinity(parsedMin))
 437:                 _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global min_cooldown_seconds=\"{minRaw}\"> is not finite — falling back to {minSeconds}s");
 438:             else if (parsedMin < 0f)
 439:                 _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global min_cooldown_seconds=\"{parsedMin}\"> must be >= 0 — falling back to {minSeconds}s");
 440:             else if (parsedMin > seconds)
 441:                 _logger.LogWarning($"CareerConfig: <Global min_cooldown_seconds=\"{parsedMin}\"> exceeds cooldown_seconds={seconds} — falling back to {minSeconds}s");
 442:             else
 443:                 minSeconds = parsedMin;
 444:         }
 445: 
 446:         return new GlobalTuning(seconds, minSeconds);
 447:     }
 448: 
 449:     private static int ParseInt(XElement el, string attrName, int defaultValue)
 450:     {
 451:         var val = el.Attribute(attrName)?.Value;
 452:         if (val == null) return defaultValue;
 453:         return int.TryParse(val, NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var result)
 454:             ? result : defaultValue;
 455:     }
 456: 
 457:     private static float ParseFloat(XElement el, string attrName, float defaultValue)
 458:     {
 459:         var val = el.Attribute(attrName)?.Value;
 460:         if (val == null) return defaultValue;
 461:         // Phase 9b #128 P2 — reject NaN/Infinity. Pre-fix only CooldownSeconds had this guard
 462:         // (Career #31 fix); generic ParseFloat fed Duration/Radius/MaxCharge/DamageBonus etc.
 463:         // NaN propagates: ExpiresAt = currentTime + NaN → IsExpired always false; NaN Radius →
 464:         // all distance comparisons false. See feedback_clamp_nan_infinity_propagates.md.
 465:         if (!float.TryParse(val, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var result))
 466:             return defaultValue;
 467:         if (float.IsNaN(result) || float.IsInfinity(result))
 468:             return defaultValue;
 469:         return result;
 470:     }

   1: namespace TAOM.Features.CareerSystem.Abilities;
   2: 
   3: // Per-frame ability activation state machine extracted from CareerPerkMissionBehavior.OnMissionTick
   4: // (Issue #102). Owns the V-key polling, ready-state one-shot flag, and charging-message throttle.
   5: // Returns an AbilityActivationResult flags struct that the host MissionBehavior translates into
   6: // InformationManager calls and ExecuteAbilityEffect dispatch -- the controller never touches
   7: // TaleWorlds statics.
   8: public interface IAbilityActivationController
   9: {
  10:     AbilityActivationResult Tick(float dt, string heroStringId, bool hasCareer);
  11:     void Reset();
  12: }
  13: 
  14: // Issue #102 deep-review MED — multi-outcome per tick. Pre-refactor the legacy mission behavior
  15: // could emit BOTH the green "ability ready" toast AND the yellow "activated" toast in the same
  16: // frame (e.g., the ability becomes ready and the player V-presses on that exact same frame); a
  17: // single-outcome enum silently dropped the ready toast. The flags struct preserves the legacy
  18: // UX behavior.
  19: public struct AbilityActivationResult
  20: {
  21:     // Cooldown just finished THIS frame; emit the green "ability ready" toast. Re-arms after each
  22:     // activation. Set independently of Activated -- both can fire on the same frame.
  23:     public bool JustBecameReady;
  24: 
  25:     // V was pressed THIS frame while the ability was ready; ExecuteAbilityEffect should run AND
  26:     // the yellow "{ability} activated!" toast should display.
  27:     public bool Activated;
  28: 
  29:     // V was pressed while on cooldown and the 2-second charging-message throttle window allowed
  30:     // a new message; emit the gray "still charging - Ns remaining" toast. Mutually exclusive with
  31:     // Activated by construction (a V-press is either Activated or Charging, never both).
  32:     public bool Charging;
  33: }

  11: {
  12:     private readonly IMutationCalculatorRegistry _calculatorRegistry;

  15:     private static readonly Dictionary<string, PropertyInfo> PropertyCache

  17: 
  18:     public MutationService(IMutationCalculatorRegistry calculatorRegistry, IModLogger logger)
  19:     {
  20:         _calculatorRegistry = calculatorRegistry;
  21:         _logger = logger;
  22:     }
  23: 
  24:     public AbilityTemplateData MutateAbility(
  25:         AbilityTemplateData template,
  26:         ICareerHeroAdapter hero,
  27:         ICareerDataService dataService,
  28:         ICareerRegistry registry)
  29:     {
  30:         if (template == null) return null;
  31: 
  32:         var clone = new AbilityTemplateData(template);
  33:         var choiceIds = dataService.GetChoiceIds(hero.StringId);
  34: 
  35:         foreach (var choiceId in choiceIds)
  36:         {
  37:             var choice = registry.GetChoice(choiceId);
  38:             if (choice == null) continue;
  39: 
  40:             foreach (var mutation in choice.Mutations)
  41:             {
  42:                 if (!string.Equals(mutation.TargetTemplateId, template.Id, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
  43:                     continue;
  44: 
  45:                 ApplyMutation(clone, mutation, hero);
  46:             }
  47:         }
  48: 
  49:         // Also apply root choice mutations if not already in choiceIds
  50:         var careerId = dataService.GetCareerStringId(hero.StringId);
  51:         var career = careerId != null ? registry.GetCareer(careerId) : null;
  52:         if (career != null && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(career.RootChoiceId))
  53:         {
  54:             var rootChoice = registry.GetChoice(career.RootChoiceId);
  55:             if (rootChoice != null)
  56:             {
  57:                 var alreadyIncluded = dataService.GetOrCreateData(hero.StringId).HasChoice(career.RootChoiceId);
  58: 
  59:                 if (!alreadyIncluded)
  60:                 {
  61:                     foreach (var mutation in rootChoice.Mutations)
  62:                     {
  63:                         if (!string.Equals(mutation.TargetTemplateId, template.Id, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
  64:                             continue;
  65:                         ApplyMutation(clone, mutation, hero);
  66:                     }
  67:                 }
  68:             }
  69:         }
  70: 
  71:         return clone;
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     private void ApplyMutation(AbilityTemplateData target, MutationDefinition mutation, ICareerHeroAdapter hero)
  75:     {
  76:         var prop = GetCachedProperty(mutation.PropertyName);
  77:         if (prop == null)
  78:         {
  79:             _logger.LogWarning($"Mutation: property '{mutation.PropertyName}' not found on AbilityTemplateData");
  80:             return;
  81:         }
  82: 
  83:         if (prop.PropertyType != typeof(float))
  84:         {
  85:             _logger.LogWarning($"Mutation: property '{mutation.PropertyName}' is not float (is {prop.PropertyType.Name})");
  86:             return;
  87:         }
  88: 
  89:         var currentValue = (float)prop.GetValue(target);
  90:         var calculatedValue = _calculatorRegistry.Calculate(
  91:             mutation.CalculatorId, currentValue, hero, new MutationParams(mutation.Params));
  92: 
  93:         // The calculator already handles the operation (flat adds, multiply multiplies, etc.)
  94:         // So the calculated value IS the final value.
  95:         float newValue = calculatedValue;
  96: 
  97:         prop.SetValue(target, newValue);
  98:     }
  99: 
 100:     private static PropertyInfo GetCachedProperty(string propertyName)
 101:     {
 102:         if (PropertyCache.TryGetValue(propertyName, out var cached))
 103:             return cached;
 104: 
 105:         var prop = typeof(AbilityTemplateData).GetProperty(propertyName,
 106:             BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.IgnoreCase);
 107: 
 108:         PropertyCache[propertyName] = prop;
 109:         return prop;
 110:     }
 111: }

The mutation semantics are now clear: `flat` is `baseValue + value`, so the new XML’s `value="-6"` produces `CooldownReduction == -6`. Since `AbilityEffectExecutor` applies only `> 0`, the rewritten choices currently do not shorten cooldown at all. I’m checking whether there are additional test gaps or wiring regressions beyond that.

**Findings**

[HIGH] Main/_Module/ModuleData/career_system/taom_career_choices.xml:82 and Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/AbilityEffectExecutor.cs:67 — #104 cooldown reduction is dead — The rewritten XML emits `CooldownReduction` as negative values (`-6`, `-9`), but `AbilityEffectExecutor` only applies reductions when `template.CooldownReduction > 0f`. `BuiltInCalculators.flat` is `baseValue + value`, so these mutations produce `-6`/`-9`, not positive reductions. I counted `50` `-6`, `48` `-9`, and `0` positive `CooldownReduction` entries. Fix: make the XML/script emit positive `6`/`9`, or explicitly invert negative XML values before calling `ApplyCooldownAdjustment`; add an end-to-end mutation test for a real choice. Phase 3e RCA: prior review validated `AdjustCooldown` with positive direct values but did not trace XML value -> flat calculator -> mutated template -> executor guard.

[LOW] Main/Features/CareerSystem/Abilities/AbilityEffectExecutor.cs:64-84 — Cooldown is shortened before effect success — After the sign fix above, `ApplyCooldownAdjustment` will run before `executor.Execute(context)`. If the executor throws, the ability has already activated and its cooldown has already been shortened, but no activation toast/sound/particle completes. Fix: move the cooldown adjustment after `executor.Execute(context)` and before the toast/sound block; the HUD still sees the adjusted cooldown on the next tick. Phase 3e RCA: the earlier review focused on keeping `registerContext` before `Execute` for partial buff restores, but did not separately audit the new cooldown side effect’s failure ordering.

[LOW] Main/Features/CareerSystem/Domain/AbilityTemplateData.cs:9 and Main/Features/CareerSystem/CareerConfigProvider.cs:311 — Dead `MaxCharge` template surface remains — `AbilityTemplateData.MaxCharge` is still parsed/copied and still reflectively mutable, but production ability creation hardcodes `ChargeType.CooldownOnly` and `maxCharge: 0f` in `CareerAbilityService.cs:40-44`. Current shipped XML has no `max_charge` / `MaxCharge`, so this is latent, but future XML can target `MaxCharge` and silently do nothing. Fix: remove `AbilityTemplateData.MaxCharge` and the `max_charge` parser/copy path, while keeping `CareerAbility.MaxCharge` only if charge-based domain tests are intentionally retained. Phase 3e RCA: the fix removed the data entries but did not inventory the remaining schema/model surfaces for dead configurable fields.

**Cleared Checks**

No surviving `AbilityActivationOutcome` references. Source grep shows the only production `IAbilityActivationController.Tick` caller is `CareerPerkMissionBehavior.cs:67`. `Activated` and `Charging` are mutually exclusive by construction: the ready branch sets `Activated` and returns before the charging branch.

`min_cooldown_seconds="-5"` and `min_cooldown_seconds > cooldown_seconds` are rejected by code at `CareerConfigProvider.cs:438-441`. `min_cooldown_seconds="0"` is accepted if paired with a valid `cooldown_seconds`.

HUD cleanup’s null ownership guard is safe: `_attachedScreen != null && _hudLayer != null` short-circuits. Resetting `_hudInitialized=false` in `finally` is the right default; keeping it true would strand the singleton after a failed teardown.

XML rewrite was mechanically narrow: `git diff --numstat` reports exactly `98` additions and `98` deletions for `taom_career_choices.xml`, all mutation replacements. The script regex will not match future `value="-20.5"` because it requires the closing quote after `-20`/`-30`.
